actions: implemented continuously driven stochastic query environment with separate nuisance q and context-switch h
added fixed-uniform and generic leaky-softmax controls
swept adaptive timescales across coarse and high-noise/low-hazard grids
confirmed selected regimes with 512 common-random-number paired realizations and bootstrap intervals

material_result: Finite gain adaptation helps cumulative Hamming loss only in sufficiently nuisance-dominated tested environments and loses value as true-switch hazard rises. Generic leaky-softmax often matches or exceeds astrocyte replicator, so no replicator-specific benefit is established. In q=0.9,h=0.1 the no-adaptation/fixed-uniform control is effectively Pareto-favored; in q=0.75,h=0.02 leaky tau=10 lowered paired Hamming by 0.132 bits versus fixed-uniform but increased false switching and reduced switch-resolution rate.
exact_next_action: Replace additive beta*u with Betteti et al. 2025 source-defined input-driven Hopfield/saliency coupling and rerun q/h Pareto tests against replicator, instantaneous, fixed-uniform and generic/adaptive leaky controls.
